messages:
olivia: FYI ap-southeast1 had a ~30-45m window where many GPU jobs were getting evicted. Pattern looks like scheduling failures + short node Unreadies. :grimacing:
raj: any kube events pasted?
olivia: scheduler: `FailedScheduling: 0/28 nodes are available: 14 Insufficient nics, 8 node(s) didn't match Pod's nodeAffinity, 6 node(s) had taints the pod didn't tolerate.` Also saw kubelet evicting pods with reason: NodeNotReady and sometimes OOMKilled for sidecars.
dana: Insufficient nics usually indicates conntrack/connectivity issues rather than actual NIC hardware count. Did we push any warm-pool or scaling jobs?
olivia: Yes, warm pool autoscale for batch-infer triggered ramp after a spike. I also grabbed `conntrack -S` snapshot from gpu-apse1-07: entries=64890, table-size=65536.
raj: That is dangerously close. What's nf_conntrack_max?
olivia: `sysctl net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max => 65536` on those nodes.
dana: When conntrack hits high water it can cause conntrack drops and transient NetworkUnavailable, which makes kubelet mark NodeNotReady and triggers PDB-respecting evictions. Explains the mix of preempt/oom churn.
raj: Short-term mitigation: increase nf_conntrack_max and restart kube-proxy on a couple nodes in a rolling manner. But that's bandaid.
olivia: Agreed. I'm voting for: (1) roll bump to 200k on ap-southeast1-b only for now, 2 nodes at a time, (2) add alert: conntrack_usage > 80% over 5m, (3) schedule RFC for scheduler policy to prefer nodes with conntrack headroom for bursty gangs.
dana: Also consider adding a nodeCondition taint when conntrack_usage > 90% so scheduler drains bursty pods away. That avoids confusing this with GPU fragmentation.
raj: App engineers: we should push keepalive/connection-pooling to reduce ephemeral connections. I'll ping product owners for batch-infer/docs-embedder.
sre-bot: Incident logged: INC-2026-519 ap-southeast1 conntrack pressure -> eng-infra oncall
olivia: I'll run the rolling sysctl change now on 4 low-load nodes in apse1-b, 2 at a time, and post outputs. Will follow up with a short postmortem and action items.
dana: add a Cesium dashboard tile for conntrack table usage + a per-az heatmap.
raj: long term: scheduler enhancements + infra defaults (higher conntrack max for GPU nodes) + app-level pooling.
olivia: Noting for postmortem: root cause is NIC/conntrack exhaustion from warm-pool attach/detach churn causing transient node Unreadies -> eviction & failed scheduling. Different from allocation fragmentation, but has same customer impact.
